payload.entry: LANDING REVIEW: Read this epic, both child scopes and their sole notes, plan:202611/failed_turn_handoffs.md, parent phase sase-1vn.3 and its plan. Verified sase-core commit 34461b7fd8c03405c330985b8fd658b469e564c1 and sase commit c783119ffdf81215cbeaa93bddff6f4b82334e49 against actual policy, bindings, collector, admission, cleanup, adoption and recovery code. The source pin contains the core commit. Recorded check runs ec922cf4702b03e5c523acd94b495502 and 07116f5e14ad994965fdaade68afc801 both succeeded. This landing reran 25 inactive-host tests plus 61 neighboring stranded/recovery/reconcile/contracts/reclaim tests, all passing. No check-full was run. Fetched both origins: both HEADs match their upstreams. Reviewed six non-epic sase commits since epic creation (51fc0d8cb2, 1cde333808, 5b184c837c, f6dd22d4dd, dcd6c726c3, 61d955445c) and core 7e857edd: bead collision/publication and test organization changes introduce no additional handoff consumer or conflicting ownership policy. Governing Rust/host-completion/verification decisions are honored by the broad architecture, but three acceptance gaps prevent close: (1) injected cleanup_staged_monitor OSError is swallowed, settlement marker and owner-index deletion still happen, and a second settlement returns already_settled without retrying (one cleanup call across two attempts); (2) after settlement, write_staged_handoff of questions into the same origin succeeds and overwrites its saved monitor stage; (3) inline settlement runs before done.json exists, while write_done_marker_and_update_index/finalize_loop never retries after durable failure. A local probe confirmed no settlement marker before or after terminal marker publication. These are remaining epic work; a medium tale will repair them and complete this epic and parent phase closeout. Existing questions/readopt tests cover writing a fresh file and direct receipt invalidation, so the tale also needs actual public-path integration coverage.

FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE: Neither child sase-1vn.3.1.1 nor sase-1vn.3.1.2 has a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP entry; no genuinely distinct unrelated task was discovered, so no new task or duplicate +1 is warranted. The sase-1vn.3.1.2 note recommends live reconciliation and closing sase-1sh. That is verification of this epic own incident, not a separate follow-up. Read sase-1sh in full and inspected monitor 3w69pb9ezmfy: it remains held with no elapsed execution. Resolution is deferred until the three landing gaps are fixed; the approved child plan final paragraph reserves sase-1sh closure for the containing sase-1vn land agent, so the tale should leave that agent a verified recommendation instead of closing the incident here. The historical sase-1r2.6 phase was already closed manually, so reproduce stranded/failed and blocked-ancestor behavior on an isolated open-phase fixture rather than claim its live status can flip. Separate existing scopes sase-1r4 (owned by sase-1ra), sase-1si and sase-1sj stay untouched. Epic-symbol audits for sase-1vn.3.1 and parent phase sase-1vn.3 currently return no entries. Carry these triage outcomes into the final close note.
